title: James Brown Funk — Double-Thumb Gallop (Open Hammer Pop)
description: The classic Wooten open-hammer-pop technique, creating a dense 16th note gallop. The thumb strikes down on the open E string, the left hand hammers a fretted note, and the index finger pops the octave.
focus: The thumb must push entirely *through* the string and rest on the A string below it, rather than bouncing off, to set up the upstroke (if used) or to allow the pop.

title: James Brown Funk — Groove Call-and-Response
description: Treat the first bar as a statement and the second as an answer. Avoid filling the rests just because you can.

description: Alternate root, octave, fifth and octave to build a stronger melodic groove than a single-register root pattern.

title: James Brown Funk — Pentatonic Octave Melody
description: Combine octave displacement with a major pentatonic vocabulary so the groove becomes melodic without losing its root-centered identity.

title: James Brown Funk — R&B Ghost-Note Pocket
description: Treat silence and low-volume attacks as equal parts of the groove. The represented rests create the rhythmic skeleton; add muted ghost notes physically on the instrument.

title: James Brown Funk — Rocco Prestia Tower Fingerstyle 16th Engine
description: Relentless muted 16th-note staccato fingerstyle engine driving Tower of Power style funk.

title: James Brown Funk — Sixteenth-Note Anticipation into the One
description: Place the next chord root slightly early so the bassist pulls the groove forward without filling every beat.

title: James Brown Funk — Syncopated Chromatic Approach (Motown Style)
bookReference: Standing in the Shadows of Motown
description: A signature James Jamerson-style bassline featuring heavy syncopation (anticipated beats), chromatic approach notes, and strategic dead notes to propel the groove forward.
focus: The rhythmic placement is crucial. The 'push' onto beat 3 happens a 16th note early (the 'ah' of 2). Notice the chromatic walk up into the IV chord.
